{{Short description|American statistician and computer scientist}}
'''Rebecca Willett''' is an American statistician and computer scientist whose research involves [[machine learning]], [[signal processing]], and [[data science]]. She is a professor of statistics and computer science at the [[University of Chicago]].{{r|profile}}

Willett has a Ph.D. in electrical and computer engineering from [[Rice University]], completed in 2005. She worked as a faculty member in electrical and computer engineering at [[Duke University]] from 2005 until 2013, when she moved to the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].{{r|profile}} She moved again to the University of Chicago in 2018.{{r|alum}}

Her research has included machine learning methods for the analysis of corn crop quality,{{r|silage}} and weather patterns.{{r|forecast}} She was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] in the 2021 class of fellows, "for contributions to mathematical foundations of machine learning, large-scale data science, and computational imaging",{{r|sf}} and an [[IEEE Fellow]] in 2022 "for contributions to the foundations of computational imaging and large-scale data science".{{r|fieee}} In 2022, she was elected Vice Chair of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] Activity Group on Imaging Science (SIAM SIAG/IS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIAM Activity Groups Election Results |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-activity-groups-election-results-56 |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=SIAM News |language=en-US}}</ref>
